title: Retail Sales Cleanup & Reporting
basisNote: Rubric built from public sources (Microsoft MO-200 skills outline). Trainer co-sign planned in the pilot.
reviewNote: Trainer co-sign is planned for the pilot and has not yet happened.

sources.title: Filter data in a range or table in Excel

checks.name: Workbook Structure & Required Sheets
checks.mappingNote: Practical evidence: Sales_Data and Summary sheets exist with required columns. Conceptual evidence: explaining workbook vs worksheet tabs.
checks.acceptableEvidence: Valid macro-free .xlsx workbook containing both Sales_Data and Summary sheets with exact header columns.

levels.0: Not evident: Workbook is unreadable, macro-enabled, or missing Sales_Data / Summary sheets.
levels.1: Partially evident: Both sheets exist, but header names or column order deviate from specification.
levels.2: Demonstrated: Valid .xlsx with both required sheets and all 5 expected header columns.

checks.name: Duplicate Order Removal
checks.mappingNote: Practical evidence: unique Order ID count matches seed expectation. Conceptual evidence: explaining how duplicate rows skew totals.
checks.acceptableEvidence: All duplicate Order ID rows removed so unique row count equals expected seed count (16).

levels.0: Not evident: Duplicate Order IDs remain or valid unique rows were deleted.
levels.1: Partially evident: One duplicate removed, but at least one duplicate Order ID remains.
levels.2: Demonstrated: Zero duplicate Order IDs remain and all 16 unique orders are preserved.

checks.name: Customer Name Hygiene
checks.mappingNote: Practical evidence: zero leading/trailing spaces in Customer Name cells. Conceptual evidence: explaining =TRIM or cell cleanup.
checks.acceptableEvidence: Customer Name cells contain no leading/trailing spaces and use consistent title casing.

levels.0: Not evident: Leading/trailing whitespace or lowercase inconsistencies remain across most rows.
levels.1: Partially evident: Spaces trimmed on most rows, but casing or 1-2 rows remain uncleaned.
levels.2: Demonstrated: 100% of Customer Name cells are trimmed and properly cased.

checks.name: ISO Date Standardization
checks.mappingNote: Practical evidence: all Date cells parse to YYYY-MM-DD. Conceptual evidence: explaining why consistent date formats enable sorting.
checks.acceptableEvidence: Every cell in the Date column follows ISO YYYY-MM-DD string or valid Excel date serial.

levels.0: Not evident: Mixed date formats (DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY.MM.DD) remain uncleaned.
levels.1: Partially evident: Most dates standardized, but 1-3 rows remain in mixed text formats.
levels.2: Demonstrated: All 16 Date cells are normalized to ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

checks.name: Missing Values & Numeric Currency
checks.mappingNote: Practical evidence: blank categories imputed as General and Amount stored as numeric. Conceptual evidence: explaining number vs text formatting.
checks.acceptableEvidence: Blank categories filled with 'General' and all Amount values stored as numeric values without 'Rs.' text prefixes.

levels.0: Not evident: Text prefixes remain in Amount or blank categories remain empty.
levels.1: Partially evident: Numeric amounts fixed, but blank categories left empty (or vice versa).
levels.2: Demonstrated: All blank categories imputed and all Amount values stored as clean numbers.

checks.name: Summary Formulas (=SUM, =AVERAGE, =COUNTIF)
checks.mappingNote: Practical evidence: Summary sheet contains live =SUM, =AVERAGE, and =COUNTIF formulas. Conceptual evidence: explaining why formulas are preferred over hardcoded totals.
checks.acceptableEvidence: Summary sheet uses live =SUM, =AVERAGE, and =COUNTIF formulas referencing Sales_Data ranges.

levels.0: Not evident: Summary cells are blank or contain hardcoded numbers instead of formulas.
levels.1: Partially evident: =SUM is present, but =AVERAGE or =COUNTIF formulas are missing or reference wrong ranges.
levels.2: Demonstrated: Live =SUM, =AVERAGE, and =COUNTIF formulas present with accurate range references.
